name: TypeScript Conductor Agent Reusing Existing Vercel AI SDK tool() Definitions
query: We have a TypeScript service with a couple of Vercel AI SDK `tool()` definitions using zod schemas — `getForecast` and `getAlerts`. Build a Conductor agent called `weather_bot` that reuses those tool definitions as they are. Show me how to run it once from the command line and how we'd deploy it.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agents.md (decision table → path 3 'bring your framework', TypeScript column), references/agent-sdks.md (TypeScript install/import matrix; Vercel AI row: AI-SDK `tool()` objects go straight into `Agent.tools`), and examples/agent-deploy-and-invoke.md.
Step 2: Preflight — `conductor agent list` and `GET /api/providers/status` to pick a `provider/model` whose provider is configured on the server.

Step 3: WebFetch the JavaScript SDK `docs/agents/` before pinning; for unchanged `parameters`-based tools install `npm i @io-orkes/conductor-javascript ai@4 zod@3`. For AI SDK 5+, use Conductor's native `tool()` adapter with `inputSchema`.

Step 4: Code: `import { Agent, AgentRuntime } from "@io-orkes/conductor-javascript/agents"`; keep the existing `tool({ description, parameters: z.object({...}), execute })` objects unchanged and pass them into `new Agent({ name: "weather_bot", model: "openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions, tools: [getForecast, getAlerts] })` (array or map form).
Step 5: `run.ts`: `const runtime = new AgentRuntime(); const result = await runtime.run(agent, "Forecast for Seattle?"); console.log(result); await runtime.shutdown();`.

Step 6: Deploy vs serve split: `deploy.ts` calls `runtime.deploy(agent)` (registers only, prints `requiredWorkers`); `serve.ts` calls `runtime.serve(agent)` as the long-lived process that executes the `tool()` `execute` functions. State the worker gate.

Step 7: Environment: the JS SDK 4.x reads `CONDUCTOR_SERVER_URL` (ending in `/api`), `CONDUCTOR_AUTH_KEY` / `CONDUCTOR_AUTH_SECRET` (plus `CONDUCTOR_TLS_*` / `CONDUCTOR_PROXY_URL`), or takes them explicitly as `new AgentRuntime({serverUrl, keyId, keySecret})`; provider keys stay on the server. Never invent `AGENTSPAN_*` names.
Step 8: Tests via `@io-orkes/conductor-javascript/agents/testing` (`mockRun`, `expectResult`), noting `mockRun` executes every tool locally (a wiring check, not a routing check).
Step 9: Invocation from a workflow uses `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"` and `name: "weather_bot"` — never `agentType: "vercel_ai"`. Never recommend `conductor deploy`.
success_criteria: Install includes `@io-orkes/conductor-javascript` and either pins `ai@4 zod@3` for unchanged `parameters`-based tools or uses the native Conductor `tool()` adapter for AI SDK 5+ — no invented package such as `@conductor/vercel` or `conductor-vercel-ai`
Imports `Agent` / `AgentRuntime` from the `@io-orkes/conductor-javascript/agents` subpath (not the package root, not `agentspan`)

The user's Vercel AI SDK tool definitions are reused with their zod schemas intact — either passed directly as AI-SDK v4 `tool()` objects (Zod `parameters` + `execute`) or re-declared with the native Conductor `tool(execute, {name, description, inputSchema})` — and the agent mentions the AI SDK 5+ `inputSchema` detection caveat or the auto-generated tool-name caveat (N/A and passing if the plan uses the native `tool()` with explicit names)
`model` is a provider-qualified `provider/model` string (e.g. `openai/gpt-4o-mini`), set explicitly
The one-off run script calls `runtime.run(agent, prompt)` and then `runtime.shutdown()` (or an equivalent close) so the process exits

Deploy and serve are separate: `runtime.deploy(agent)` registers, `runtime.serve(agent)` runs the tool workers as a long-lived process — with an explicit statement that without `serve()` tool calls hang

Runtime configuration is honest: `CONDUCTOR_SERVER_URL` / `CONDUCTOR_AUTH_KEY` / `CONDUCTOR_AUTH_SECRET` env (or the same values passed explicitly to `new AgentRuntime(...)`), with provider keys on the server — no invented env names
Tests (if included) import from `@io-orkes/conductor-javascript/agents/testing` (`mockRun`, `expectResult`) — no invented `conductor agent test`
`agentType: "vercel_ai"` (or any framework name) never appears; any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` with `name: "weather_bot"`
The plan WebFetches the JS SDK `docs/agents/` before pinning versions and never recommends `conductor deploy`
